Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to meet up at the Erasmus office to get some papers and my student ID. That part was easy, but I was also around several places to get an APHP number (a personal number for staff at the hospitals), which was impossible. I ended up never getting the number.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They handle a lot of things last minute, so don't get stressed if everything isn't in order before departing.

questions.answer:
Exploring the city, museums, concerts. 
Going to other cities in France - Grenoble, Normandy, Champagne, Bordeaux.

questions.answer: Easy

questions.answer: I didn't very much, the medical students were very busy with studying.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Culture of going out on cafes, restaurants, bars.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Don't stress about things not being in order before departure. 
2) It is a great opportunity to learn a new language, but you need to insist on speaking French if you want to learn it, as many people want to be nice to you and speak English instead to make it easier. 
3) I think that 12 weeks of clinical exchange in the same department was too much. I would have liked to split it up on two different departments if possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to apply for many scholarships, because it is very expensive to live in Paris.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of nice people and exploring Paris. Learning to speak French.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be in a foreign hospital with a different culture.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
